finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY clause: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query. An attacker can inject SQL via ORDER BY (e.g. boolean/blind subqueries using CASE WHEN, or error/timing-based extraction) to read arbitrary data from any table in the SQLite DB. Stacked queries are generally not run via PDO sqlite query(), but blind exfiltration of other tables is still possible.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' — taken from the request with no validation
$sort concatenated into the SQL string and executed via PDO::query; ORDER BY cannot be parameterized, and no allowlist is applied

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or escaping on this path. Compare list_users_safe (list.php:10-11), which uses an allowlist map, and find_user (list.php:16-17), which uses a prepared statement with a bound parameter. Neither is applied in list_users_sorted. No auth check is present in the file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query() call with no allowlist, cast or escaping, unlike list_users_safe at list.php:10-11; the file has no auth check and the function is not called elsewhere in the directory, so reachability depends on a caller outside it.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] straight into the ORDER BY of a PDO query with no allowlist, cast or auth check; the allowlist in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11) is not used by list_users_sorted.
